name: Accent Hold
description:
Type accented and special characters the macOS way: hold a letter (e, a, c, o, n …) and pick its accented variant (é è ê ë, ç, ñ, ô …) from a popup next to the text cursor, with its number, the arrows or the mouse. A quick tap types the letter as usual, and the held letter does not repeat. Works on any keyboard layout (AZERTY, QWERTZ …), without a daemon or root.

For applications that do not use the GNOME input method, a configurable shortcut (Super+E by default) opens the same picker: type the base letter, then choose the variant.

Preferences: press-and-hold on/off and duration, shortcut, character table, active keyboard layouts.

Clipboard use: the shortcut picker inserts the chosen character by briefly putting it on the clipboard and sending Shift+Insert, then restores your previous clipboard content. Nothing is read or kept otherwise.
